newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday July 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday July 8.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* European Union finance ministers gave their seal of approval to Italy's plan for meeting the requirements for economic and monetary union (EMU), while warning that further economics measures may be needed (all).

* Marco Pannella, Radical party secretary, handed out wads of cash (2.7 billion lire) to passersby in the northeastern town of Treviso in protest at the use of taxpayers' money to finance political parties (all).

* Bank of Italy Governor Antonio Fazio said that despite very low inflation in Italy the outlook for economic growth was very uncertain. According to the Governor, what was putting a break on investments was an excessive tax burden and excessive regulation above all of labour (all).
* Prime minister Romano Prodi admitted the Italian fiscal burden was excessive but said it was too early to cut taxes (all).

* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi reaffirmed Italy was ready to resort to further measures to respect EMU criteria if necessary. While stressing the importance of welfare state reforms, Ciampi also said the EU commission showed particular appreciation for Italy's progress on inflation (all).
* Piedmont International, the company which owns Olivetti Personal Computers, is expected to inject 65 million dollars into the company (all).

* Luigi Maranzana, the new managing director of Istituto Bancario San Paolo di Torino, presented a reforming programme to the board of the banking group. Italy's largest commercial bank would be completly restructured with the main aim to offer "better value for shareholders" (Sole 24 Ore).

* Aereoporti di Roma, the state-controlled company which runs Rome's airport, said it would present its privatisation and development plans on Tuesday. The group will be the first Italian airport company to come on the stock market (Corriere della Sera).
* Italy's Finmeccanica and Britain's General Electrics Co Plc said that their discussions on co-operation in the defence sector were continuing successfully (Corriere della Sera).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
